problems.title: A median to a right triangle’s hypotenuse
problems.question: The leg opposite 30° and the hypotenuse total 15 cm. Find the median to the hypotenuse.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: The short leg is half the hypotenuse; the hypotenuse median is also half the hypotenuse.
steps: If the hypotenuse is c, then c+c/2=15, giving c=10. The median is 5 cm.

problems.title: Circumradius from leg sum and inradius
problems.question: A right triangle’s legs total 34 and its inradius is 4. Find its circumradius.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
steps: 4=(34−c)/2 gives c=26. Thus R=13.

problems.title: An angle from a median and a perpendicular bisector
problems.question: In right ABC, CM is the hypotenuse median, K is midpoint of CM, N lies on MB, MN=BC and NK is perpendicular to MC. Find BAC.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: $MC=MB$; points on the perpendicular bisector of MC satisfy NM=NC.
steps: Let ABC=beta. Since NC=MN=BC, triangle BCN has equal BC,CN, so CBN=BNC=beta.
M,N,B are ordered on the hypotenuse. Thus MNC=180−beta, and isosceles MNC has NMC=beta/2.
In isosceles MCB, CMB=180−2beta. This is also NMC, so beta/2=180−2beta. Hence beta=72° and BAC=18°.

problems.title: An exterior angle between two secants
problems.question: In the diagram two secants meet outside a circle. Their farther intercepted central arc is 128° and nearer arc is 40°. Find the exterior angle.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Exterior secant angle = half the difference of intercepted arcs.
steps: The difference is 128−40=88°. Half is 44°.

problems.title: Two tangents and an inscribed triangle
problems.question: Two tangents meet outside the circle. The inscribed triangle has the other two angles 86° and 40°. Find the tangent-ray angle.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Inscribed angle is half its opposite arc; tangent-ray angle is 180° minus the minor central angle.
steps: The third triangle angle is 180−86−40=54°. It subtends the arc between tangent points, measuring 108°.
The tangent angle is 180−108=72°.

problems.title: An angle between a radius and a chord
problems.question: The source inscribed triangle has base angles 56° and 72°. A radius from its top vertex is drawn. Find its angle with the chord to the 72° vertex.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: An inscribed 56° angle gives a 112° central angle; two radii make an isosceles triangle.
steps: The radius triangle subtending that chord has apex 112°. Its two base angles are (180−112)/2=34°.
The marked radius-chord angle is one of these.

problems.title: An altitude to a diameter
problems.question: In the figure two upper chords are equal, their inscribed triangle has a base angle 36°, and a perpendicular is dropped from the top vertex to a diameter. Find its angle with the right upper chord.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Equal chords give equal triangle base angles; a diameter subtends a right angle.
steps: Label the top vertex T, right diameter endpoint R, and the other endpoint D. The left upper base angle is 36°, so TDR=36°, as both subtend chord TR.
Triangle DTR is right at T. Thus TRD=54°. The right triangle formed by T, R and the perpendicular foot has top angle 90−54=36°.

problems.title: A tangent and a secant through a cyclic quadrilateral
problems.question: Use the source diagram: cyclic A,B,D,C have ABD=118°; secant A,D,P and tangent PC make 54° at P. Find DAC.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Inscribed angle = half its intercepted arc; exterior tangent-secant angle = half the far-arc minus near-arc difference.
steps: Arc ADC opposite B is 236°. Put arc DC=t, making arc AC through the upper side 236−t.
At P, 54=[(236−t)−t]/2, giving t=64°. Angle DAC subtends DC, so it is 32°.

problems.title: Tangent-chord angle beside a diameter
problems.question: In the diagram DB is a diameter and ACB=56°. Find the acute angle between the tangent at A and chord AD.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Arc AB=2ACB; a semicircle measures 180°; tangent-chord angle is half its arc.
steps: Arc AB=112°, so arc AD on that semicircle is 180−112=68°. The marked tangent-chord angle is half, 34°.

problems.title: Four arcs in a specified cyclic order
problems.question: Two chords divide a circle into arcs in cyclic ratio 3:2:5:8. Find the smaller angle between the chords.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: An intersecting-chord angle is half the sum of opposite intercepted arcs.
steps: One ratio unit is 360/18=20°. Opposite arc sums are (3+5)20=160° and (2+8)20=200°.
The two intersection angles are 80° and 100°; the smaller is 80°.

problems.title: Distances to perpendicular chords
problems.question: Perpendicular chords AB,CD meet at K with AK=2,KB=9,CK=3,KD=6. Find the sum of distances from the centre to the chord lines.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: The centre lies on both chord perpendicular bisectors.
steps: The two line distances are 1.5 and 3.5, totaling 5.

problems.title: A quarter equals a fifth
problems.question: Two numbers total 27 and one-fourth of the first equals one-fifth of the second. Find their product.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
steps: Nine ratio units total 27, so the numbers are 12 and 15. Their product is 180.

problems.title: A linear equation containing a parameter
problems.question: Solve $0.3x-2(0.1x+2a)=4(a-1)$ for x.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Distribute brackets, then collect x terms.
steps: The equation becomes 0.1x−4a=4a−4. Thus 0.1x=8a−4 and x=80a−40.

problems.title: A quotient of a cube and a square
problems.question: Evaluate $(125x^3-75x^2y+15xy^2-y^3)/(25x^2-10xy+y^2)$ at x=0.2,y=2.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: The numerator is (5x−y)³ and denominator (5x−y)².
steps: At the given values 5x−y=1−2=−1, nonzero. Cancel its square to get the value −1.

problems.title: Infinitely many solutions to a linear system
problems.question: For which a does $3x+ay=12$, $9x-15y=36$ have infinitely many solutions?
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: The second equation must be three times the first.
steps: The x coefficient and constant already have factor 3. Require 3a=−15, giving a=−5.

problems.title: Substitute a known solution into a parameter system
problems.question: (−1,1) solves $bx+2ay=1$, $(3a-1)x-by=1$. Find a+b.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Substitute x=−1,y=1 into both equations.
steps: We obtain −b+2a=1 and −3a−b=0. Thus b=−3a and 5a=1.
a=1/5,b=−3/5, so their sum is −2/5=−0.4.

problems.title: A cancelled factor still restricts a function’s domain
problems.question: Where is $y=(2|x|-4)/[(x^2-9)(|x|-2)]$ undefined?
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: The original denominator must be nonzero.
steps: x²−9 vanishes at ±3 and |x|−2 at ±2. All four are excluded, even though the numerator also vanishes at ±2.

problems.title: Read slope and intercept from a graph
problems.question: Identify the source graph: it slopes down at 45° and crosses the y axis at 2.7.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Slope $m=-\tan45^\circ=-1$; line equation y=mx+b.
steps: With intercept b=2.7, the equation is y=−x+2.7.

problems.title: An intersection abscissa fixes a parameter
problems.question: $y=ax+12$ and $y=(3-a)x+a$ meet at x=2. Find a.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: At a common x the two y expressions are equal.

problems.title: Two workers with different work times
problems.question: Two workers together finish in 2.4 hours. One hour by the first and three by the second complete 75%. Find the second worker’s solo time.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Let rates u,v be jobs per hour: u+v=1/2.4=5/12; u+3v=3/4.
steps: Subtraction gives 2v=3/4−5/12=1/3, so v=1/6. The solo time is 1/v=6 hours.

problems.title: Three concurrent lines
problems.question: For which a do y=2x−1,y=−2x+3,y=4x+a pass through one point?
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: First intersect the two parameter-free lines.
steps: 2x−1=−2x+3 gives (x,y)=(1,1). The third line contains it iff 1=4+a, giving a=−3.

problems.title: Evaluate the right branch of a piecewise function
problems.question: $f(x)=x-2$ for x≥3 and $f(x)=7-3x$ for x<3. Find f(5)−f(−5).
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Choose the formula using the input condition.
steps: f(5)=3. Since −5<3, f(−5)=7+15=22. The difference is −19.

problems.title: A shaded half-plane with an unlabelled slope
problems.question: The sketch shades above a negative-slope line y=kx. Which of A=(−1,2),B=(−5,3),C=(−3,−2) lie in it?
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Above the line means y>kx. For k<0, A requires k>−2 and B requires k>−3/5; C never satisfies it.
steps: The drawing suggests a slope between −2 and −3/5, in which case only A is above the line.
But the line has no numerical slope, scale or labelled point. For k=−1 only A qualifies; for k=−1/2 both A,B qualify; for k=−3 neither qualifies.
Therefore the listed “only A” reflects the intended drawing, while the stated numerical information does not determine the answer.
problems.answer: Intended sketch: only A; strictly, insufficient numerical information.
problems.note: The plotted dot is unlabelled and the axes have no scale. A precise half-plane classification cannot be established solely from the negative slope.

problems.title: An identity from a sum of squares
problems.question: x²+y²=1. Evaluate x⁶+3x²y²+y⁶.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: $u^3+v^3=(u+v)^3-3uv(u+v)$, with u=x²,v=y².
steps: x⁶+y⁶=1−3x²y². Adding 3x²y² leaves 1.

problems.title: Compose and shift a linear function
problems.question: f(x)=2x−1. Solve f(f(x))+2f(x−1)=7.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
